questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes use arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a solid yellow arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
It means you can turn in the direction the arrow points.
It means a green arrow will appear next.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same thing as a yellow traffic light. Slow down and get ready for a red light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: It is only a suggested speed.
You must drive at exactly this speed or get a ticket.
This is the maximum safe speed in good weather and road conditions.
This is the maximum safe speed in all weather and road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: This is the maximum safe speed in good weather and road conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the highest legal speed for that road. You may need to drive slower than the limit. When conditions are bad, you should slow down.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the road angles toward the center. What does this mean?

options.text: An intersection is coming up.
You are approaching a construction area.
You will need to turn left soon.
The road will become narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will become narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the edge of the road marks the road's boundary. When the edge line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads, which vehicle must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: If a car is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: Honk to get the other driver's attention. If they don't move, steer right to escape. Steering left is dangerous because the other driver might also swerve left. Always brake hard and steady. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: When turning onto a one-way street, you should:

options.text: Always turn into the right lane.
Always turn into the left lane.
Turn into the lane that disrupts traffic the most.
Turn into the lane that disrupts traffic the least.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn into the lane that disrupts traffic the least.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that interferes the least with other traffic. Do not make a dangerous turn.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed on curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's inertia can make it hard to turn. You must slow down before entering a curve to stay in control.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, you should:

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply to the left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up even with the car in front of the parking space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the car in front of the parking space.
questions.explanation: Find a space, check traffic, signal, and then stop parallel to the car directly in front of your space. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: What color are the lines on the road that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines in the center of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No parking.
Divided highway ahead.
Left turn signal.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what they must do. It means you cannot park your vehicle here.

questions.question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A broken line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: On a multilane road with traffic moving in opposite directions, when should you use the shared center lane?

options.text: To pass another vehicle
To slow down or stop before turning left
As a lane for regular traffic when traffic is slow
As a parking lane

questions.correctAnswerText: To slow down or stop before turning left
questions.explanation: Use the center lane only to slow down or stop safely before making a left turn. Never use it to pass or as a regular traffic lane.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look, then go if the road is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells you to slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: Shared lanes are meant for:

options.text: Bicyclists.
Truck drivers.
Motorcyclists.
Passenger vehicle operators.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicyclists.
questions.explanation: Shared lanes help bicyclists stay in narrow lanes safely alongside cars. They show other road users where bicyclists are likely to be.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see it.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down and don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right side of the road safely and stop. Wait until you are sure the emergency vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and let other traffic go first before entering the intersection or roadway.

questions.question: At an intersection, the light turns from green to solid yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it as a caution sign and continue through.
Stop immediately.
Stop before entering, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to cross before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down and try to stop before entering the intersection. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through.

questions.question: You cannot pass other vehicles within ____ of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel.

options.text: 200 feet
100 feet
500 feet
350 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Do not pass within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel. Only pass where it is legal and safe.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to your previous lane.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you came from.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
End of construction zone.
School crossing ahead.
Flagger ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. Flaggers direct traffic in construction areas.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do?

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: A second train may be on the other track. Always check both tracks before crossing. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming from either direction.

questions.question: When may you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: You cannot cross solid yellow lines, except when making a turn. Broken lines may be crossed, but solid lines cannot.

questions.question: If a vehicle using high beams comes toward you, you should look toward ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on your path until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: All car crashes must be reported within how many days?

options.text: Five

questions.explanation: If a crash is not investigated by police and causes no injury or death, you must report it in writing within 10 days.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should generally:

options.text: Enter above the speed of traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Accelerate to the speed of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate to the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up. Signal, check for an opening, accelerate to match traffic speed, and merge safely.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and children are playing nearby. Before moving, you should:

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.
Sound your horn so the children will hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Get out and check behind your car before backing up. Mirrors alone may not show everything, especially young children.

questions.question: You come to an intersection blocked by traffic. You should:

options.text: Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
Sound your horn to make the cars move up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if you cannot drive completely through it. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. You should:

options.text: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders for other vehicles before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. Always check mirrors and signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, drivers should:

options.text: Increase their speed to reach their final destination more quickly.
Decrease their following distance.
Increase their following distance.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase their following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase the distance between your car and the car ahead when roads are wet.
